title: Developer 'Ignite' Onramp: Hosted API value props + pricing anchors
summary: A compact messaging + competitive-notes brief for a developer-first hosted API onramp program we’re calling 'Ignite'. Focus: three rapid integration paths, transparent unit economics language, latency-budget value prop, and pricing anchors that lower time-to-first-success.
content:
Purpose and audience:
This doc is a working brief for GTM + product to align on a developer-centric hosted API positioning that emphasizes speed-to-first-success, deterministic latency budgets, and cost clarity. Primary audience: individual engineers, small engineering teams trying prototypes, and platform teams evaluating managed inference for production trials.

Core hypothesis:
Developers pick hosted inference when they can: (a) integrate in <30 minutes, (b) get predictable latency at scale without guessing the infra math, and (c) model quality is backed by quick evaluation artifacts. If we package those three as a small set of promises and concrete onboarding assets, conversion and trial-to-paid velocity will increase.

Topline value props (developer-first framing) — short copy options:
- "Ship an LLM feature in 30 minutes: SDK, example app, and pre-verified model to get your first request live."
- "Predictable latency budgets—pick a latency tier, we guarantee the tail and show the cost tradeoffs."
- "Transparent token economics—per-call breakdowns and simulated monthly line-items so engineers can estimate unit cost before committing."
- "Fallbacks that keep apps online—automatic model tiering and regional routing if capacity is constrained."

Differentiated levers to highlight (internal checklist):
- Latency budgets: Tiered SLOs (fast, balanced, cost) with explicit p95/p99 targets and sample workloads to demonstrate impact on token cost.
- Unit transparency: Example invoice mockups and SDK traces that map request -> tokens -> GPU-second equivalence.
- Dev ergonomics: curated starter templates (chat, summarization, embeddings) with test prompt sets and eval scoring to compare models.
- Rollout controls: canary routes + automatic fallback to cheaper model variant on quota breaches.

Quickstart paths (3 deliberate, user-facing flows) — copy-first + dev steps:
1) "Try in 5" (zero-install cURL) — ideal for quick demos and email CTAs.
   - Headline microcopy: "First reply in 5s — paste, run, see."
   - Steps: 1) Create free account -> 2) Copy single cURL example -> 3) Watch streaming output in terminal.
   - Success metric: first API response time + retention to SDK install.

2) "Integrate in 30" (SDK + sample app) — target for product prototypes.
   - Headline: "Three files, one SDK, app-ready."
   - Steps: 1) npm/yarn install SDK -> 2) copy example chat handler (40 LOC) -> 3) run local server and see browser demo.
   - Drops to include: preselected model and a prompt profile tuned for the sample app.

3) "Scale-safe demo" (deploy with predictable latency) — target for platform/infra evals.
   - Headline: "From prototype to predictable throughput."
   - Steps: 1) select latency tier -> 2) run workload generator (provided) -> 3) view console (cost by token + latency heatmap) and toggle burst pools.

Pricing language options (framing + sample microcopy) — aim for clarity and quick mental math:
Option A — Simple PAYG with latency tiers:
- Headline: "Pay per token. Pick a latency tier."
- Microcopy: "Start with our Balanced tier to minimize cost. Upgrade to Fast tier for p95 under 150ms. Billing is tokens consumed + tier surcharge; view sample monthly bill estimator."

Option B — Credit-first developer plan + burst pools:
- Headline: "Free dev credits + predictable burst capacity."
- Microcopy: "New accounts get $200 credits and a 5-hour burst pool for prototyping. Post-credits, we bill per-token; teams can reserve Dedicated burst capacity for steady throughput."

Option C — Committed discounts for early production:
- Headline: "Commit to save—monthly reserved capacity with committed discounts."
- Microcopy: "If you commit 1M tokens/month, get 30% unit discount and access to a dedicated throughput pool with SLA-backed latency."

Pricing anchors and tactics to test (A/B matrix ideas):
- Anchor A: show a 3-month sample invoice for a typical chat product at 500k tokens/mo.
- Anchor B: show per-1000-token price prominently vs per-request price (test which is more intuitive).
- Anchor C: highlight "cost to prototype" (how far $200 credit goes) on the sign-up flow.

Competitive notes (short, tactical) — what to call out vs each competitor type:
- Versus model-access marketplaces (simple model access): call out Redwood’s runtime optimizations and cost levers (batching/caching) that lower per-token cost for real workloads. Show a comparison: identical model raw latency vs Redwood latency with batching and caching.
- Versus managed endpoint providers (cloud AI features): emphasize developer ergonomics + observable dev-first metrics (token breakdowns, prompt-level tracing) and quickstarts.
- Versus self-hosted inference stacks: highlight predictable SLOs, no infra ops for burst capacity, and explicit fallback policies—avoid arguing raw peak perf.

Example competitive snippets for sales enablement:
- "They give you a model; we give you predictable latency and the math that explains your monthly bill."
- "If your product needs to stay up during bursts, our routing + burst pools keep the UX smooth without manual autoscaling runs."

Example page copy + microcopy (for landing + pricing):
- Hero line: "Build with LLM latency you can budget for."
- Subline: "Hosted inference for teams that want clear unit economics and fast time-to-first-success."
- CTA primary: "Try with $200 credits"; secondary: "Compare latency tiers"
- Pricing page callout: "Estimate your bill" with a small input: tokens/month -> shows estimated monthly $ and % savings with commitment.

Onboarding artifacts we must ship for Ignite:
- 1-page cheat sheet: cURL + SDK snippet + triage checklist.
- Starter repo: chat app + summarizer + embedding search with preloaded test prompts and eval harness.
- Console demo route: example project ID prepopulated with telemetry to show cost/latency breakdown.
- Evaluation kit: 50 curated prompts + scoring script so devs can baseline model quality quickly.

Measurement plan (KPIs):
- Time to first API response (median) for new accounts.
- % of new accounts that run the SDK quickstart within 24 hours.
- Trial-to-paid conversion at 30 and 90 days.
- Average cost estimate accuracy (ratio of predicted vs actual bill) after 1 month.

Suggested experiments (first sprint):
- Test two home page CTAs: "$200 credits" vs "Integrate in 30 minutes" and measure sign-ups and quickstart completions.
- Pricing microcopy A/B: per-1000-token price vs example-invoice anchor.
- Latency-tier offering: roll Balanced vs Fast to 50/50 and measure upgrade-to-dedicated attempts.

Open questions for product/engineering:
- What exact p95/p99 targets can we guarantee for each tier on public hosted region X? (need SRE confirmation).
- Can we produce on-demand simulated invoice examples from the console before billing is enabled?
- What guardrails do we enforce for burst pools for new accounts to avoid large unpaid usage?

Next steps (owners + timeline):
- GTM copy freeze (Priya) + sample pages: 1 week.
- Starter repo + eval kit (Solutions Eng + DevX): 2 weeks.
- Console mock for estimate tool (Product + Instrumentation): 3 weeks.

Notes (scratchpad):
- Consider a badge "Latency budget verified" for partner apps that pass our probe tests.
- Email drip idea: Day 0: $200 credit + cURL; Day 2: SDK quickstart; Day 7: estimate your bill; Day 14: invite to production pilot.
- Slack thread refs: #prod-onboard, #pricing-experiments.

References and links (for internal reviewers):
- Existing quickstart drafts in Drive (to iterate): /shared_drives/go-to-market/first-5-minutes-developer-onramp-voice-experiments.json (used as background)
- Open product tickets: ENG-1428 (sample workload gen), PRD: PROD-590 (latency tiers)

Author notes: this is intentionally prescriptive and product-forward — draft intended to feed a 2-week sprint with PS/DevX to produce the assets developers need to get their first meaningful integration completed.

-- end of brief --
